source_refs.note: Exercise 5.2, Question 2 (book p. 158); answer key PDF 306

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find the angle from the line with slope \(m_1\) to the line with slope \(m_2\), where \(m_1 = 2\), \(m_2 = -\frac{1}{2}\).
blocks.explanation:
The slopes are given directly.
Before using Theorem 7, look at \(1 + m_1 m_2\): if it is 0 the lines are perpendicular.
Plan: test \(m_1 m_2\), then state the angle.
steps:
Given: \(m_1 = 2\), \(m_2 = -\frac{1}{2}\).
To find: the angle \(\theta\) from the first line to the second.
Method: Theorem 7 needs \(1 + m_1 m_2 \ne 0\); Corollary 2 says the lines are perpendicular when \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\).

Find \(1 + m_1 m_2\)
\[m_1 m_2 = 2 \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -1\]
\[1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\]
Why: the denominator of Theorem 7 is zero, so \(\tan\theta\) is undefined.

Conclusion
\[\theta = 90^\circ\]
Why: Corollary 2: \(\ell_1 \perp \ell_2\) iff \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\).

Check:
The slopes \(2\) and \(-\frac{1}{2}\) are negative reciprocals of each other, the usual sign of perpendicular lines \(\checkmark\)

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find the angle from the line with slope \(m_1\) to the line with slope \(m_2\), where \(m_1 = 3\), \(m_2 = -2\).
blocks.explanation:
Slopes are given; \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 1 - 6 \ne 0\), so Theorem 7 applies.
Plan: put the values in \(\tan\theta = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2}\) and read the angle.
steps:
Given: \(m_1 = 3\), \(m_2 = -2\).
To find: the angle \(\theta\) from the first line to the second.
Method: Theorem 7.

Apply Theorem 7
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{-2 - 3}{1 + (3)(-2)}\]
\[= \dfrac{-5}{-5} = 1\]
Why: \(m_2 = -2\) comes first in the numerator; both top and bottom are negative, so the result is positive.

Read the angle
\[\theta = \tan^{-1} 1 = 45^\circ\]
Why: \(\tan 45^\circ = 1\) and a positive tangent gives an acute angle.

Check:
\[\tan 45^\circ = 1 \;\checkmark\]
In the other order the formula gives \(\tan\theta = -1\), i.e. \(135^\circ = 180^\circ - 45^\circ\), as expected.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key also prints a part '(iii) \(120^\circ\)'. Question 2 has only parts (i) and (ii), so that line belongs to no printed part. The keys for (i) \(90^\circ\) and (ii) \(45^\circ\) are correct.
